Deann Hurst Does it work? The results of castor oil inducing labor are mixed. A small study published in Alternative Therapies of Health and MedicineTrusted Source revealed that over half of those dosed with castor oil went into active labor within 24 hours. This is compared to only 4 percent beginning labor in the same timeframe without any treatment.  But another larger study, published nearly 10 years later in the Australian and New Zealand Journal of Obstetrics and GynaecologyTrusted Source, again looked at using castor oil.  It determined that while there were no harmful effects associated with castor oil to either mother or baby, it wasn’t particularly helpful at inducing labor, either.  When it’s effective at beginning labor, castor oil may cause irregular and painful contractions, which can be stressful to mom and baby alike. This can lead to exhaustion.  It may also cause your baby to pass meconium, or their first stool, before delivery. This can be problematic after birth
